<l0/> already uses this hook. Call it yourself when you render your own <l1/>, such as a chat composer or an inline editor.
Height changes animate over 180ms, and a change that comes in mid-animation starts from the current height, so fast typing never jumps. Under reduced motion the height snaps.
It listens for `input` on `window` and only measures. It never reads or writes the value, so keystrokes are never delayed or dropped.
It refits when the width changes, because text that wraps differently changes the height.

On each change the hook sets the height to `auto`, reads the natural `scrollHeight`, and clamps it to the element's own CSS `min-height` and `max-height`. All of that happens before paint, so you never see the collapsed frame. The bounds stay in your CSS, so they can be responsive or use `lh` to count lines.
On touch screens, use at least 16px text in the textarea, or iOS zooms in when it's focused.
Past `max-height` the textarea scrolls. Otherwise its scrollbar stays hidden, so it doesn't flash on each new line.
Set `rows={1}` and `resize-none`. A manual resize handle fights the automatic height.
The controlled value. Pass undefined for uncontrolled textareas.
Turning `enabled` off or unmounting removes the inline height and overflow, handing the size back to your CSS.
Typing fires `input`, but setting `value` from code doesn't. Pass the value as the third argument and the textarea refits when you insert a template or clear it.
useAutosize: auto-resizing textarea hook for React
